title: Command and Mediator
idea: Command turns a request into an object you can store, queue and undo. Mediator routes talk between many objects through one hub, so none references another.
points: A command holds its receiver (the object doing the work) and arguments.
An invoker, like `History`, runs commands and keeps them on a stack for undo.
Colleagues, the objects the mediator connects, hold only its interface and report to it.
The mediator holds the rules, so changing how widgets interact touches one class.

hero.title: Undo and redo are two stacks

steps.caption: `run` calls `execute` on the first command, then pushes it on the undo stack.
The second command runs the same way and lands on top.
`undo` pops the top command, calls its `undo`, and pushes it on the redo stack.
`redo` pops from the redo stack, calls `execute` again, and moves it back.
Undo once more: the `world` command waits on the redo stack again.
Running a new command clears the redo stack. That undone branch is gone.

code.title: Command
code.caption: Each edit is an object, so `History` can undo and redo it later.

walk.text: The command contract: do the work, and reverse it.
`Document` is the receiver. It knows nothing about commands or history.
`Append` stores its receiver and text, which is all it needs to undo.
`History` is the invoker. A new command clears the redo stack.
Undo and redo move one command between the two stacks.
`main` runs two edits, undoes one, then redoes it.

code.title: Mediator
code.caption: Two inputs and a button never reference each other. The dialog decides.

walk.text: The mediator interface: widgets only report that they changed.
Each widget holds the mediator, updates itself, then calls `changed`.
The button has no idea which fields exist.
`SignupDialog` owns the rule: valid email and ticked terms enable submit.
`main` changes the widgets; every reaction goes through the dialog.

pitfalls: Store what `undo` needs inside the command at run time, not in shared fields.
Watch the mediator's size: when it holds every rule, it becomes a god class.
Skip Command for one-off calls with no undo, queueing or logging need.

quiz.why: Two undos empty the undo stack; the third does nothing. The redo stack's top is `ab`, undone last, so redo re-applies it.

takeaway: Command makes an action an object; Mediator makes one hub own the interactions.
